senses.definition: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see look, through.
senses.example: He looked through the binoculars at the bird.

senses.definition: To take a view of the contents of; search in, either with the eyes or by hand.
senses.example: I looked through the magazine, but it didn't seem very interesting.

senses.definition: To penetrate with the understanding; to see through.
senses.example: I got a small ring to make; when I brought back the finished trinket to him he stared at me with his sparkling eyes, as if he would look through my very soul, and then said: 'Thou art a clever expert fellow […]

senses.definition: To appear or pretend not to see something or someone who is clearly visible.
senses.example: I tried to get Michele's attention at the party, but she looked right through me!
